newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - May 16.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Briefing - May 16.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

MUNICH - Private broadcasters accuse government officials and media authorities of overregulating their industry while allowing print media more freedom in the advertising they carry. The president of the Association of Private Broadcasting and Telecommunications, Juergen Doetz, calls for swift deregulation of the German market at the Munich Advertising Conference. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Digital television service DF1 has won its legal battle with Premiere for permission to advertise for customers outside the southern state of Bavaria, the Hamburg regional appellate court decides. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - The Hamburg-based advertising agency KNSK replaces the Phoenix agency of Duesseldorf for the account of pay-television channel Premiere. (Horizont)
DUESSELDORF - Chemical giant Bayer is looking for an advertising agency to handle a global image campaign. (Advertising Age)

DUESSELDORF - Despite a weak business climate, the conference market managed to post gains for 1996 with rented congress space climbing 2.2 percent from the previous year, says the managing director of the conference association Auma, Hermann Kresse.
FRANKFURT - The Frankfurt-based advertising agency Lowe & Partners will stop representing cigarette brand Stuyvesant and be replaced by Springer & Jacoby of Hamburg. (Horizont)
